clues.text: In the citadel of Susa, he questioned his brother Hanani and men from Judah about Jerusalem.
Told that Jerusalem's wall was broken down and its gates burned, he wept, fasted, and prayed for days.
When the people wept at hearing the Law read, he told them, "The joy of the LORD is your strength."
This son of Hacaliah was the first to seal the written agreement made by Israel's leaders, Levites, and priests.
Seeing Jerusalem large but with few people, God moved him to gather the nobles and people to be enrolled by genealogy.
He served as governor of Jerusalem in the days of Joiakim son of Jeshua, alongside Ezra the priest and scribe.
In his days and the days of Zerubbabel, all Israel gave daily portions for the temple singers and gatekeepers.
